trust_decision.summary: How much header-block data a remote HTTP/2 peer may make Ember buffer and decode is decided in H2Connection.readLoop (CONTINUATION accumulation into headersInProgress/pushPromiseInProgress) and in Hpack.decodeHeaders (decoded header-list size). At the pinned commit neither has a byte, list-size or time bound, and the h2 settings come from ConnectionSettings.default with maxHeaderListSize = None.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'unbounded continuation frame accumulation', and this line appends each non-final CONTINUATION frame to headersInProgress without a size check.

fix_sites.entry_point: EmberServer HTTP/2 (ALPN h2, h2c prior knowledge, h2c upgrade): HEADERS without END_HEADERS starts accumulation; fix adds a receive-headers timeout (fix.diff:361-364)
EmberClient withHttp2: server sends PUSH_PROMISE without END_HEADERS; fix adds the same timeout (fix.diff:390-395)
EmberClient withHttp2: completing a PUSH_PROMISE continuation cleared the wrong field (headersInProgress); fix clears pushPromiseInProgress (fix.diff:279-280)
Every HTTP/2 header decode (server requests, client responses, push promises); fix adds decoded-size accounting with the 32-byte overhead and a truncation check (fix.diff:695-724)
Hpack.create, called by H2Server/H2Client; fix makes the decoder limit a parameter instead of a fixed 65536 (fix.diff:670-678)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The h2c Upgrade escalation (ServerHelpers.scala:529-537) and the client builder look like a legacy path and a different product (client talking to a server it chose), so a solver who caps continuation accumulation in H2Connection can argue these are out of scope. Likewise, a solver who adds the Hpack decode cap can argue raw CONTINUATION byte buffering is already bounded, because the decode step rejects the result.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A legitimate header block split across HEADERS + several CONTINUATION frames (for example large cookies within maxHeaderSize), and HPACK dynamic-table indexed references, must still be reassembled and decoded. Rejecting CONTINUATION outright, using a cap below maxHeaderSize, or skipping decode on reject (which desyncs the shared HPACK table) breaks valid requests. A normal slow but legitimate client must also not be killed by the stall/receive timeouts.

O6_input_shapes: HEADERS (no END_HEADERS) followed by an endless or slow CONTINUATION stream on the server (receive-headers timeout)
PUSH_PROMISE followed by CONTINUATION frames toward the client
single HEADERS frame whose HPACK block decodes to a header list larger than maxHeaderSize
HPACK indexed references that are small on the wire and large when decoded (the 32-byte per-entry overhead is counted, fix.diff:705-707)
decoder-truncated header block (the endHeaderBlock truncation flag, fix.diff:720-724)
the same shapes via h2c prior knowledge and h2c Upgrade as well as ALPN h2
